drafted_from: tool:generate-a-checklist-from-my-text row (tools/workflows/tool-rows.json), tools/workflows/do-work/checklist_gate.py, and tools/workflows/test/test_checklist_gate.py (test_check_passes_until_the_text_changes), run on its made-up bakery library
start_here: Say to your AI: "I changed one row of my written checklist in ./bakery-library/checklist-source.md. Run tool:generate-a-checklist-from-my-text with --check against ./bakery-library/schema.json, and if the file differs, write it and check it for problems."
no_lists_because: It reads a checklist you wrote as a text file and writes one generated checklist file beside it, so it reads and writes no list.
instructions: 1. Keep your checklist as one text file (one section per stage, one table row per check, notes that annotate a check) and a schema file whose checklist_source part holds the regular expressions that say how your text is laid out; the text is the only source.

2. Say to your AI: "Run tool:generate-a-checklist-from-my-text". It reads the row with tools:list {"tool":"tool:generate-a-checklist-from-my-text"}, then runs its command from the root of your Workshop checkout: python3 tools/workflows/do-work/checklist_gate.py --library <your library folder> --schema <your schema file> checklist <mode>.
3. After you edit the text, run it with --check. Exit 0 and {"all_passed": true} means the file on disk matches your text; exit 1 says in words which checks differ.

4. When it differs, run it with --write to regenerate the file ({"written", "checks", "must"}), then with --problems, which finds repeated ids, a required flag that is not true or false, a per-item check with no rule, a phase that names no check and counts that do not add up.
5. Never edit the generated file by hand; change your text and run it again. Exit 2 means your text or schema could not be read, and the error names what to fix.

worked_examples.title: One changed row is found, written, and the file checks clean
worked_examples.ask: I changed one row in my written checklist. Does the checklist file still match it?
worked_examples.given: From tools/workflows/test/test_checklist_gate.py (test_check_passes_until_the_text_changes) on its made-up bakery library, run for real: after `checklist --write` the library holds 12 checks, 9 of them required. In ./bakery-library/checklist-source.md the row "| B2.2 | [ ] Sold out by close | all | Count the shelf | habit | no |" is changed to end with "| yes |". The command the person's AI runs is: python3 tools/workflows/do-work/checklist_gate.py --library ./bakery-library --schema ./bakery-library/schema.json checklist --check
worked_examples.hands_back: Exit status 1 and the last JSON line {"all_passed": false, "difference": "./bakery-library/checklist.json is not what checklist-source.md generates. Only in the generated file: []; only in checklist-source.md: []; differing: ['B2.2']. Edit checklist-source.md and regenerate."}. Running the same command with --write then answers {"written": "./bakery-library/checklist.json", "checks": 12, "must": 10}, and with --problems answers {"all_passed": true, "problems": []}.
